hints: Focus on the trend in acid-base character of Period 3 oxides when they react with water, from strongly basic on the left to strongly acidic on the right.
Sort the oxides given into basic (Na2O, MgO), insoluble with no effect (Al2O3), and acidic (P4O10, SO3) and think what pH each would give alone.
To finish with a pH just below 7, you need an acid and a base that almost cancel each other out, leaving the solution only very slightly acidic.
walkthrough:
**Recall the Period 3 oxide trend**

Think left to right across Period 3. Basic character decreases and acidic character increases.

$\text{Na}_2\text{O}$, $\text{MgO}$ are basic, $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is insoluble and amphoteric so has no effect on pH, and $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$, $\text{SO}_3$ are acidic.

**Write what each oxide does in water**

A soluble basic oxide gives an alkali with high pH. An acidic oxide gives a strong acid with low pH.

$$\text{Na}_2\text{O} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{NaOH, pH about 13-14}$$
$$\text{MgO} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Mg(OH)}_2, \text{pH about 9-10}$$
$$\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10} + 6\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 4\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4, \text{pH about 0-2}$$
$$\text{SO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4, \text{pH about 0-2}$$

**Test the mixtures for pH just below 7**

Two bases can only give pH well above 7. Two acids can only give pH well below 7.

Only a combination of one strong base and one strong acid can neutralise to give a solution that is almost neutral but still just acidic, which matches $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ with $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$.

options.A: Incorrect. MgO is sparingly soluble to give Mg(OH)2 with pH about 9, while Al2O3 is insoluble and does not affect pH. The mixture would be alkaline, pH above 7, not just below 7.
options.B: Incorrect. Both Na2O and MgO are basic oxides. Na2O gives strongly alkaline NaOH and MgO gives weakly alkaline Mg(OH)2, so the mixture must have pH well above 7.
options.C: Correct. Na2O forms a strong alkali and P4O10 forms a strong acid. Together they can neutralise each other: NaOH + H3PO4 to form a salt solution. With a slight excess of acid, the pH ends up just below 7.
options.D: Incorrect. Both SO3 and P4O10 are acidic oxides forming H2SO4 and H3PO4. The mixture would be strongly acidic with pH 0 to 2, far more acidic than just below 7.
